newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 30.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:
* Indonesia's ruling Golkar party headed for a landslide general election victory, taking 73.87 percent of the votes counted by 7:50 a.m. (0050 GMT) on Friday.
* On Thursday, the Dow Jones industrial average dropped 27.05 points to 7,330.18 after falling 26 points Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange as technology issues took a beating.
MARKET

* Jakarta stocks closed sharply higher on Thursday, Indonesia's election day, on heavy buying in blue chip counters led by heavyweight Telkom, brokers said. The index rose 17 points, or 2.53 percent, to close at 689.50 points.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,438.00/39.00 at 0115 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,441.00/43.00.
STOCKS TO WATCH

* Heavyweight telecommunications firm PT Telkom on expectation it will announce good first quarter results due around midday (0500 GMT) Friday. Also on continued market talk that Telkom will do private placement despite a company denial.
* Toll road operator Citra Marga after a company official confirmed it planned to propose a rights issue soon.
* Fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudra on a report that Standard & Poor assigned a BB-plus rating to its subsidiary's notes.
* The country's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur following encouraging first quarter net profit of 97.37 billion rupiah, compared with 76.38 billion rupiah in the same 1996 period.
* Cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa after announcing lower first quarter net profit 89.17 billion rupiah, against 100.49 billion rupiah in the year-ago period.
* Car maker after it announced 1997 first quarter net profit of 119.83 billion rupiah, up from 73.46 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
* Retailer Multipolar and supermarket Hero on renewed market speculations that Multipolar would buy a stake in Hero in the second half this year.

* Sentiment on feedmill maker counters such as Anwar Sierad and Charoen Pokphand following reports that Indonesia's agriculture minister would seek a corn import tariff. Traders said the move, which was reported in local newspapers, took the industry by surprise.
* Polyester producer Polysindo after it announced its first quarter net profit was sharply higher at 52.20 billion rupiah, against 44.13 billion rupiah in the same 1996 period.
* Engineering firm Texmaco after it announced Q1 net up to 17.5 billion rupiah, compared with 9.1 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
* Cigarette stocks such as Sampoerna and Gudang Garam on reports the government was planning to issue regulations banning smoking in certain public places.
* Sampoerna after it announced that it first quarter net profit at 99.56 billion rupiah, compared with 84.21 billion rupiah in the same period in 1996.
* Small tourism firm Bayu Buana on market talk the firm would acquire some hotels belong to an international group.
* Surabaya-based property firm Mas Murni Indonesia on continued talk that it would make a private placement at a price of 1,200 rupiah.
